chapter: On the road with Duke and his bandmates
title: The Henderson, Texas incident
summary: In Henderson a white woman sat beside Duke; Duke was frightened and later a local took Tricky Sam's trombone to test him.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In some place in Henderson, Texas -- that was a tough town. We were playing a dance for a lot of big people in there, and some of them cowboys and so on, and one of the ladies in there came by and tried to sit down in the same seat as Duke Ellington, you know? Oh, he was scared to 'Cause there was people in the front there, too. And the fellow that was dancing with her was out there in front of the bandstand, and probably said, to himself, "I wonder what my girlfriend is sitting down talking with a nigger".

So Duke was scared, and called for Jack Boyd -- "Jack, take this lady out of here, take her out!'. So by the end of the dance, somebody picked up Tricky's trombone, they picked it up and took it with them. We was getting ready to go on the bus and it was right behind -- I mean, Tricky 's trombone, so they said, "you know, I'm gonna take this trombone with me and I don't care if you tell the police, you know? I don't give a damn about the police in there." He was a big man there in Texas -- an old man, you know? He said, "he didn't give a damn about the police coming." Duke said, "Well, if that's the way you feel about it -- there's the trombone. If you want it, go ahead and take it." That killed him when he said that, and he said, "No, it's all right; I don't want the trombone -- I all just wanted to see was how he was gonna act about it." You know?
